newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - June 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - June 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

South African minerals giant Gencor will today announce a merger of its nickel division with Australian company Queensland Nickel. The merger will create a nickel group valued at more than A$2.5 billion that controls approximately 7 per cent of the world's nickel market. Page 21

Surprise investor in food group Burns Philp & Co, New Zealand businessman Graeme Hart said yesterday that he would not insist on a company board seat, but as a major investor he hoped he would be involved in any future decisions. The comments have fuelled speculation that Hart is considering increasing his current 16.2 per cent stake in the company. Page 21

Foster's Brewing Group's wine division, Mildara Blass, has completed negotiations on two separate ventures which will allow it to produce premium wine labels in Chile and the US in partnership with local companies over the next 18 months. The expansion is expected to cost Mildara Blass A$4 million in capital outlays. Page 22.

The June quarter AICD/KPMG Boardroom Report, released yesterday, states that 64 per cent of company directors surveyed expect economic conditions to improve over the coming year. The transport-communications sector was particularly confident with over 60 per cent of executives predicting above-budget profits for the next year. Page 25.

CanWest Global Communications and four other companies that invested in the Ten Network last year have been ordered to present specific documents to the Federal Court by June 27. The documents relate to the dispute CanWest and the four other companies had with Federal Treasurer Peter Costello which led the Treasurer to order the new shareholders to sell their shares in the network. Page 26.

The Singha 1 wildcat gas exploration well in Sumatra, Indonesia, is to be abandoned by Australian oil developers Energy Equity Ltd and Novus Petroleum because of mechanical problems. Preliminary drilling has however revealed strong gas indications and the well will be returned to. Page 27.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian winery d'Arenberg yesterday announced it had paid approximately A$20,000 a hectare, or A$1.1 million in total, for a 57 hectare property located in South Australia's McLaren Vale area. The sale of the dry pasture land has confirmed the area as being one of Australia's most valued viticultural markets. Page 19.

Industry observers believe that the development of Energy Resources of Australia's Jabiluka uranium deposit in the Kakadu National Park, Northern Territory, will likely be delayed for another year due to strong opposition from local traditional owners, conservation groups and the Federal Opposition parties. ERA yesterday lodged its final environmental impact study with the Federal Government. Page 19.

A study by finance industry research group Assirt has revealed that financial planners judge mastertrust group Asgard as the best service provider currently operating in the retail investment market. Other companies ranked highly by the 400 groups surveyd include Macquarie Investment Management, BT Funds Management, AM and Connelly Temple. Page 22.

IBM Australia managing director Bob Savage said yesterday that instead of attempting to develop a technology base of its own, Australian industry should adopt the best features of other countries technology. Speaking at an Australia-Israel Chamber of Commerce lunch, Savage said that Australia only had limited experience and capital resources in this area. Page 20.

Various companies and industry associations, including Ardmona Foods, Pacific Brands and the Australian Electrical and Electronic Manufacturers Association, have united in protest against proposed Government legislation allowing Chinese companies to export large quantities of underpriced goods into Australia. Convenor of the group, and the government relations manager of agricultural chemicals manufacturer Nufarrm, Bruce McAllen said yesterday the legislation would result in the collapse of the anti-dumping system. Page 21.

The Plastics and Chemicals Industry Association warned yesterday that Federal Government inertia on tax reform was putting investments worth approximately A$6 billion at risk. The projects specifically named by the industry body included A$4 billion worth of investment in an integrated chemicals complex in the North West Shelf, and a A$2 billion project aimed at bringing existing chemical plants to world scale. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Analysts predict that BHP will post net profits of over A$1.4 billion when it announces results for the last financial year next week. The past year has been a important one for BHP with the company closely examining its long-term strategy and making a number of important decisions, including the closure of the Newcastle steelworks. Page 29.

Pay TV company Australis Media has requested its two major shareholders - Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting and US based Lenfest - to increase their funding commitment over the coming months as discussions on restructuring the pay TV industry coninue. The need for increased capital was accentuated by last month's Supreme Court decision disallowing an infrastructure sharing deal between Australis and Optus Communications. Page 29.

Sydney Harbour Casino has abandoned plans to buy land next to its permanent site, despite awareness that it needs to acquire more space to build extra five-star accommodation. The land is owned by Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting company. Page 1.

AM Corporation has launched a new non-superannuation masterfund in response to demand from investment advisers for such an investment vehicle. The new fund will be called LifeTrack Investment Service, and it is expected to garner between A$100 million an A$120 million from high net worth investors. Page 31.

The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) has significantly downgraded its forecasts for farm production and exports in light of how the El Nino effect is expected to cause drought conditions across Australia. However ABARE's epections for record high minerals and energy exports remain unchanged. Page 33.

An Australian Bureau of Statistics survey released yesterday shows a 5.8 per cent jump in the building of new homes in the March quarter. Most of this new construction took place in New South Wales and Victoria. Page 33.
THE AGE

Australian Financial Institutions Commission figures released yesterday show that net profits for Australia's 275 credit unions remained steady at A$107 million for the nine months to March 31. Credit Union Services Corporation chief executive Vern Harvey conceded that the rate of growth was slow but that assets and members were still increasing. Page B2.

New Zealand based Brierley Investments is believed to have started adding to its 19.9 per cent stake in media group John Fairfax Holdings. Brierley is using the "creep" provisions under the Corporations Law, which allow a 3 per cent increase in holdings every six months without this being considered a take-over attempt if the holdings rises above the twenty per cent takeover threshold. Page B2.

Figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics show that Victoria is increasing its share of Australian business investment. Trend levels of investment have increased by 13 per cent in the March quarter from a year ago, with all areas of industry sharing in the rise. Page B3.

Australian food giant Goodman Fielder yesterday received approval from the New Zealand Commerce Commission for its proposed buy-up of Defiance Industries' New Zealand milling and baking operations. Goodman Fielder is expected to consider a further purchase to replace its Meneba NB holdings, which it sold earlier this year for A$312 million. Page B4.

Telstra suggested yesterday that an agreement between it and News Corp over Telstra's plan to reduce its Australian cable roll-out could be announced within the next few days. Industry observers predict Telstra could pay up to A$100 million in compensation to News Corp for the scaled back cable roll-out. Page B5.

Ansett is set to sign a memorandum of understanding with Singapore Airlines, allowing joint ventures between the two companies. One consequence of the agreement would be Singapore Airlines expending hundreds of millions in investment in the financially troubled Ansett in return for a one-third holding. Page B5.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
